description: Switch Helping Hands' north-star model from a plain VLA to a WORLD ACTION MODEL (a model that jointly predicts future world state — video/frames — and robot actions). This updates the north star in voice-4858e8fa (MolmoAct2-style zero-shot manipulation from a camera plus a plain-language instruction): the goal stays the same, only the model family changes. Research current open world action models (late 2026), pick one that fits the project (open weights, runs on our hardware, camera + language in, actions out), and write a plan for the switch: what replaces the MolmoAct2 path, integration steps, and what we lose/gain. Ref: voice-4858e8fa.

results.identified_issue: Research/plan item, no product code. Surveyed late-2026 open WAMs: FLUX 3 Action (BFL, 7B, released 2026-09-23, native LeRobot policy lerobot.policies.flux3, SO-101 checkpoint black-forest-labs/flux-3-action-so101, scene/wrist camera keys, 30 Hz LeRobot v3 data, 42-action chunks executing 32; FLUX Kommunity License = commercial OK under $5M revenue); Cosmos 3 Nano Policy (NVIDIA 16B, OpenMDW, no SO-101 embodiment or LeRobot support); DreamZero-SO101 (Wan2.1-14B LoRA, only imagined rollouts, no closed-loop real-arm result); GigaWorld-Policy/Motus/LVP/VideoVLA (no SO-101). Key honesty point: FLUX publishes no SO-101 zero-shot number; its SO-101 demo used ~200 teleop episodes of LoRA, so the switch trades MolmoAct2's published 56.7% zero-shot for a fine-tune-expected path — flagged prominently. Unverified: inference VRAM (only 'RTX 5090' stated), whether their normalisation quantiles/calibration match our follower (MolmoAct2 needed a sign flip; FLUX documents none), latency without async/RTC inference in a split Mac/GPU-box setup, and LeRobot's page itself says this revision still needs GPU+robot validation. Nothing run on hardware. molmoact2.md got a superseded-note pointer; its camera/GPU/app sections still apply.
results.summary: Wrote a plan to switch the north star to FLUX 3 Action, a world action model with an SO-101 checkpoint already in LeRobot.
results.detailed_description:
The plan is in plans/world_action_model.md. My pick is FLUX 3 Action from Black Forest Labs, which came out last week. It's a 7B world action model with an SO-101 checkpoint that's already built into LeRobot, and it uses the same scene-plus-wrist camera pair we'd already planned. It also leads the open models on the benchmarks. Cosmos 3 Nano has a cleaner license but doesn't support our arm. DreamZero-SO101 has only ever been shown imagining rollouts, never driving a real arm.

The honest loss: MolmoAct2 has a published zero-shot number on our arm, and FLUX doesn't. Their SO-101 demo used about 200 teleop demos. So plan on fine-tuning, not zero-shot. The license is also no longer Apache. It's free for us while revenue is under $5M.

The gain: better results per demo, and the model can draw the frames it expects to happen. That means the app could show "here's what I'm about to do" before the arm moves, and you tap go or stop.

The one repo change is recording at 30 Hz through lerobot-record with both cameras, in place of record_actions.sh. Then it's a rented NVIDIA box, the stock checkpoint on pick-and-place, and about 50 demos for a LoRA. Nothing has been run on hardware. Say go and I'll start on the recording change.
